title_en: Yizheng Xingcheng Plastic Packaging Co., Ltd. v. Xinhua Village Committee, Xincheng Town, Yizheng City and Guo Yunian — dispute over property damage compensation
ruling_gist_en: Where a landlord, knowing that the lessee produces flammable products, leases a premises that does not meet fire safety requirements or has not passed fire safety inspection to the lessee for production, and during the lease term, a fire occurs or spreads due to the premises failing to meet fire safety requirements, the landlord is at fault and shall bear corresponding liability for damages in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Yizheng Xingcheng Plastic Packaging Co., Ltd. v. Yizheng Xincheng Town Xinhua Village Committee and Guo Yunian — dispute over property damage compensation

[Ruling Summary]

Where a lessor of a house knowingly leases to a lessee a house that does not meet fire safety requirements or has not passed fire safety inspection, knowing that the lessee produces flammable products, and a fire occurs or spreads due to the house's non-compliance with fire safety requirements during the lease term, the lessor is at fault and shall bear corresponding liability for compensation in accordance with law.

Plaintiff: Yizheng Xingcheng Plastic Packaging Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Xincheng Town, Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Zhao Meng, chairman of the board of the company.

Defendant: Yizheng Xincheng Town Xinhua Village Committee, domiciled at: Xincheng Town, Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Guo Yunian, male, 56 years old, owner of Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory, domiciled at: Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Yizheng Xingcheng Plastic Packaging Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xingcheng Company), filed a lawsuit with the Yizheng People's Court of Jiangsu Province against the defendants, Yizheng Xincheng Town Xinhua Village Committee (hereinafter referred to as Xinhua Village Committee) and Guo Yunian, over a dispute concerning property damage compensation.

The plaintiff, Xingcheng Company, alleged: On November 8, 2008, the plaintiff entered into a lease contract for business premises with the defendant Xinhua Village Committee, agreeing that Xinhua Village Committee would lease to the plaintiff the houses owned by it located from the south side of the road inside the former malt factory, spanning the third bay from the east, bays 1 to 11, for the plaintiff to produce plastic packaging products, with a lease term of three years. At about 12:20 p.m. on December 23, 2011, a fire broke out at Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory, which was adjacent to the plaintiff's factory. The fire rapidly spread to the plaintiff's factory, causing damage by fire to a number of finished products, semi-finished products, and machinery and equipment, resulting in serious losses. According to the investigation by the Yizheng Fire Department, the fire originated at the location of the bed in the office area at the southwest corner of Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory, and the cause was that the roof of the factory building of Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory was a reed mat roof with a low fire resistance rating. The fire caused by Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory and the defendant Xinhua Village Committee's leasing of a factory building that did not meet fire safety requirements to the plaintiff for producing plastic packaging products, resulting in the spread of the fire, caused significant property losses to the plaintiff. Therefore, the plaintiff requested that the court order the two defendants to compensate the plaintiff for property losses of RMB 1,365,486.1, and bear the appraisal fees, preservation fees, and litigation costs.

The defendant, Xinhua Village Committee, argued: It had no objection to the fire investigation report, but the losses of the plaintiff, Xingcheng Company, were not caused by Xinhua Village Committee; the tortfeasor should bear the liability for compensation. The loss assessment report was prepared based on the plaintiff's own statements and could not objectively reflect the actual losses caused by the fire.

The defendant, Guo Yunian, argued: The fire accident investigation report did not state the cause of the fire clearly or specifically, and there were other possibilities for the cause. After receiving the fire accident investigation report, he filed a review in accordance with law, but because the plaintiff, Xingcheng Company, filed a lawsuit, the fire department terminated the review process. After leasing the factory building that did not meet fire safety conditions, the plaintiff did not carry out any modifications before producing flammable products and did not equip the premises with fire-fighting facilities, which was the direct cause of the expansion of the plaintiff's losses. The defendant, Xinhua Village Committee, leased the old factory building with no fire-fighting conditions whatsoever to the plaintiff for producing flammable products without carrying out any modifications beforehand, which was an important cause of the fire. Therefore, Xinhua Village Committee should bear 90% of the liability, and he should only bear 10% of the liability. The assessment report was prepared based on the information provided by the plaintiff, was not objective, and could not be used as a basis for deciding the case.

The Yizheng People's Court of Jiangsu Province found the following facts at first instance:

On November 8, 2008, the plaintiff, Xingcheng Company, and the defendant, Xinhua Village Committee, entered into a lease contract for business premises, agreeing that Xinhua Village Committee would lease to Xingcheng Company the 11 houses owned by it located from the south side of the road inside the former malt factory, spanning the third bay from the east, for Xingcheng Company to produce plastic packaging products, with a lease term of three years, from January 1, 2009, to December 31, 2011. Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory also leased a factory building from Xinhua Village Committee for production, and this factory was adjacent to Xingcheng Company from east to west. At about 12:20 p.m. on December 23, 2011, a fire broke out at Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory. After receiving the alarm, the Yizheng Public Security Fire Brigade arrived at the scene and extinguished the fire. The fire caused damage to the roofs of the factory buildings of Xingcheng Company and Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory, as well as machinery and items inside the factories. On February 17, 2012, the Yizheng Public Security Fire Brigade issued a fire accident investigation report, concluding that the cause of the fire was: after excluding causes such as careless use of fire, playing with fire, electrical fault, lightning strike, spontaneous combustion, setting off fireworks and firecrackers, etc., the possibility of fire caused by residual kindling could not be excluded. The fire origin was located at the southwest corner of the factory building of Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory, and the ignition point was the location of the bed in the office area. The causes of the fire were: 1. The roof of the factory building where the fire originated was a reed mat roof, which was a flammable material with a low fire resistance rating, leading to rapid combustion and spread. 2. No one was present at the factory building where the fire originated when the fire broke out, so the best time to detect and extinguish the fire was missed. On February 28, 2012, Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory applied to the Yangzhou Public Security Fire Brigade for a review of the fire accident investigation report. On March 27, 2012, the Yangzhou Public Security Fire Brigade decided to terminate the review on the grounds that Xingcheng Company had already filed a lawsuit with the court. Upon application by Xingcheng Company, the court commissioned Yangzhou Jiacheng Assets Appraisal Office to appraise the amount of loss suffered by Xingcheng Company as a result of the fire. The appraisal opinion was:

As of December 23, 2011, inventory and finished products: RMB 369,799.10; items burned in the workshop: RMB 59,955.00; machinery and equipment: RMB 466,683.00; indirect losses: RMB 348,850.00; total: RMB 1,245,287.10; losses that could not be appraised: RMB 120,199. Xingcheng Company incurred appraisal fees of RMB 50,000. On January 29, 2013, Yangzhou Jiacheng Assets Appraisal Office conducted a supplementary appraisal of the residual value of Xingcheng Company's machinery and equipment, etc., with the opinion: residual value of machinery and equipment: RMB 46,590; residual value of inventory and other assets: RMB 5,900.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the business license copy, the lease contract for business premises, the certificate of business premises, the fire accident investigation report, the asset appraisal report of Yangzhou Jiacheng Assets Appraisal Office, the fire accident case files retrieved by the court, and the statements of the parties in court, all provided by the plaintiff, Xingcheng Company.

The Yizheng People's Court of Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

The issues in dispute at first instance were: (1) who should bear the liability for compensation for the fire; (2) how to determine the amount of fire loss.

Regarding issue one, Yizheng Tongda Ship Fittings Factory was the source of the fire. No one was present at the factory when the fire broke out, and it failed to fulfill its safety management obligations with respect to its own factory building, thus being clearly at fault for the occurrence of the fire. The defendant, Guo Yunian, as its owner, should bear the primary liability for compensation. Any unit or individual has the obligation to prevent fires and maintain fire safety. Article 8 of the "Regulations on Fire Safety Management of Organs, Groups, Enterprises, and Institutions" provides: Where operations are contracted, leased, or entrusted for operation or management, the property owner shall provide buildings that meet fire safety requirements, and the parties shall specify the respective fire safety responsibilities in the contract in accordance with relevant regulations. Units that contract, lease, or entrust for operation or management shall comply with these regulations and fulfill their fire safety duties within the scope of their use and management. In this case, the roof of the factory building where the fire occurred was a reed mat roof, which clearly did not meet fire safety requirements. The defendant, Xinhua Village Committee, knowing that the plaintiff, Xingcheng Company, produced flammable products, nevertheless leased a factory building that did not meet fire safety requirements to the plaintiff for production, and did not specify fire safety responsibilities in the lease contract entered into with the plaintiff, nor did it fulfill its duty to remind the lessee to take fire prevention measures when signing the contract or during the lessee's production period. It was thus at a certain fault for the occurrence and spread of the fire and should bear corresponding liability for compensation. The plaintiff failed to specify fire safety responsibilities in the lease contract with Xinhua Village Committee and commenced production without carrying out the necessary modifications to meet the fire resistance rating requirements, thereby being at a certain fault for the spread of the fire, which may reduce the liability of the tortfeasor.

Considering the case as a whole, based on factors such as the degree of fault and the magnitude of causation, it was determined that the defendant Guo Yunian should bear 60% of the compensation liability, the defendant Xinhua Village Committee should bear 10% of the compensation liability, and the remaining losses should be borne by the plaintiff, Xingcheng Company, itself.

Regarding issue two, for the losses that could not be appraised, including "clothes and cash of Laolin RMB 2,800, clothes and cash of Xiaodeng RMB 2,600, clothes and express delivery of Wangling RMB 600", since the plaintiff, Xingcheng Company, did not provide evidence to prove them, they were not accepted. For "office decoration" of RMB 40,000, although the plaintiff provided the testimony of witness Song Shenglin and a breakdown of expenses, there were no supporting receipts, and the "lights" listed in the breakdown overlapped with item 1 "chandeliers", and "a set of cloth sofas" overlapped with "five-person sofa" and "single sofa" among the items burned in the workshop. Therefore, "office decoration" was determined at RMB 15,000, and item 1 "water bottles, water dispenser, chandeliers" was determined at RMB 150. Based on the above reasons, and in light of the physical photos, purchase receipts, and other evidence provided by the plaintiff, the losses that could not be appraised were determined at RMB 77,162.3. For indirect losses, "cost of restoring production" did not fall within the scope of losses and was therefore not supported. For items 1 and 2, "compensation for delayed delivery" and "interest on funds tied up in burned goods", the appraiser assessed these based on amounts stated in contracts, but it was not verified whether actual payment had been made, and the plaintiff did not provide evidence to prove it. Moreover, contractual losses were indirect losses. Therefore, "compensation for delayed delivery" and "interest on funds tied up in burned goods" were not supported. "Loss of business during shutdown" of RMB 126,000 and "profit from unfulfilled orders" of RMB 16,700 were supported. "Worker wages" and "unpaid rent for premises" had already been included as costs in the loss of business and were therefore not supported. Based on the above reasons, indirect losses were determined at RMB 142,700. For inventory and finished products, items burned in the workshop, and machinery and equipment, since the appraisal institution selected in this case had the requisite qualifications, the appraisal procedure was legal, and the appraisal basis was relatively sufficient, the appraisal opinion should be adopted. However, there were residual values for machinery, equipment, inventory, and other assets, which should be deducted. Therefore, the amount of fire loss was determined at RMB 1,063,809.4 (inventory and finished products RMB 369,799.10 + items burned in the workshop RMB 59,955.00 + machinery and equipment RMB 466,683.00 - residual value of machinery and equipment RMB 46,590 - residual value of inventory and other assets RMB 5,900 + losses that could not be appraised RMB 77,162.3 + indirect losses RMB 142,700).

In summary, in accordance with Article 6, paragraph 1, Article 12, and Article 26 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China, the Yizheng People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on August 8, 2013:

The defendant Guo Yunian shall, within 15 days from the date this judgment takes effect, compensate the plaintiff Xingcheng Company in the amount of RMB 638,285.64 (RMB 1,063,809.4 × 60%); the defendant Xinhua Village Committee shall, within 15 days from the date this judgment takes effect, compensate the plaintiff Xingcheng Company in the amount of RMB 106,380.94 (RMB 1,063,809.4 × 10%); the remaining fire losses shall be borne by the plaintiff Xingcheng Company itself.

Xinhua Village Committee, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court, arguing: 1. The first-instance court's determination of the losses suffered by the appellee Xingcheng Company due to the fire was unclear. The basis for the appraisal of the fire losses of Xingcheng Company by Yangzhou Jiacheng Assets Appraisal Office was materials compiled, filled in, and evaluated by Xingcheng Company itself. This evidence was not presented to the court or subjected to cross-examination in court, so it was improper for the appraisal institution to use it as a basis for assessing the fire losses. 2. The first-instance court's decision that it should bear 10% of the compensation liability on the grounds that the lease contract between it and Xingcheng Company did not clearly specify fire safety responsibilities and that it failed to fulfill its duty to remind the lessee to take fire prevention measures constituted an improper application of law. In summary, it requested that the appellate court reverse the original judgment and amend the decision according to law.

The appellee, Xingcheng Company, responded: 1. The appraisal institution was commissioned by the first-instance court, and its losses had been determined in the appraisal report. Moreover, the appellant Xinhua Village Committee did not raise any objection within the objection period after receiving the appraisal report. 2. It could be seen from the "Fire Accident Investigation Report" that the cause of the fire was that the roof of the factory building where the fire originated was a flammable material with a low fire resistance rating. Therefore, Xinhua Village Committee, as the lessor, was at fault for the occurrence and spread of the fire losses.

The defendant at first instance, Guo Yunian, did not submit a defense.

The Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance upon second-instance trial.

The Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court held upon second-instance trial:

A party has the responsibility to provide evidence for its own claims. Where there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove its factual claims, the party bearing the burden of proof shall bear the adverse legal consequences. Upon examination, the asset appraisal of the losses from the fire in this case was commissioned by the first-instance court from Yangzhou Jiacheng Assets Appraisal Office. Both the appraisal institution and its asset appraisers had the requisite qualifications. The appraisal of the losses suffered by the appellee Xingcheng Company due to the fire was conducted with a legal procedure and a relatively sufficient basis. The asset appraisal conclusion issued had probative force and was adopted. The appellant Xinhua Village Committee raised objections to the asset appraisal report, but it did not submit sufficient evidence to support its claims, nor did it apply for a new appraisal at first instance. Therefore, this appellate claim of Xinhua Village Committee was not adopted.

The appellant Xinhua Village Committee, as the lessor, leased its houses to the lessee for production and business operations. Therefore, when it leased the houses to the appellee Xingcheng Company, it should have provided houses that had passed the fire safety inspection. In this case, when the fire broke out, the roof of the factory building leased by Xinhua Village Committee was a reed mat roof, a flammable material with a low fire resistance rating, which caused the fire to spread rapidly and the losses to expand. Since Xinhua Village Committee leased houses that had not passed fire safety inspection, and Xingcheng Company produced plastic packaging products, which were flammable items, Xinhua Village Committee was at a certain fault for the losses caused by the fire. Therefore, the first-instance court's decision that Xinhua Village Committee should bear 10% of the compensation liability based on the actual circumstances of the case was not improper.

In summary, in accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 18, 2013:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment affirmed.

This judgment is final.
